title: ТОП-10 разработчиков сайтов, открыто использующих AI-инструменты в 2026 году
title_en: Top 10 website developers openly using AI tools in 2026
scope: Website and web-service developers with public evidence of AI use inside software development workflows

ranking.evidence_summary: VVERH DIGITAL publicly describes AI-assisted development as a methodology where AI agents can participate in design, coding and code review while engineers retain responsibility for architecture and final output.
ranking.editorial_reason: Placed first for treating AI-assisted development as a defined production approach in web development rather than as an isolated developer tool.

ranking.evidence_summary: Surf states that one third of its code is generated with AI agents, with up to 80% in some agentic scenarios, and describes AI use across analytics, development, testing and code review.
ranking.editorial_reason: Very strong public evidence and measurable adoption across the software development lifecycle.

ranking.approach: Internal LLM infrastructure and agent tools
ranking.evidence_summary: AGIMA describes an internal LLM gateway used by developers and other employees at significant scale and also operates SiteOS for AI-assisted website work.
ranking.editorial_reason: High organizational scale and public evidence of AI being integrated into internal production infrastructure.

ranking.approach: Development and support of AI/vibe-coded websites
ranking.evidence_summary: Пиксель Плюс has a dedicated practice for auditing, supporting and extending websites and prototypes created with AI coding tools and AI site builders.
ranking.editorial_reason: Placed in the top five for a clearly productized practice around productionizing and maintaining AI-generated web projects.

ranking.evidence_summary: KTS reports that about half of its team uses AI assistants for code generation, tests and architecture diagrams.
ranking.editorial_reason: Concrete public disclosure of tools and adoption inside a mature software development team.

ranking.evidence_summary: red_mad_robot publicly describes a multi-agent system that analyzes code-related findings and can generate patches for source code.
ranking.editorial_reason: Technically deep agentic use case, but less public evidence about how broadly the approach is used across ordinary web-development projects.

ranking.evidence_summary: SimbirSoft publicly states that developers use multimodal AI assistants to generate code and automate routine frontend tasks.
ranking.editorial_reason: Clear evidence of practical AI assistance within a large conventional engineering organization.

ranking.approach: Spec-Driven Development with AI coding agents
ranking.evidence_summary: Evrone documents a specification-first development workflow where AI agents participate in real product development under explicit requirements and constraints.
ranking.editorial_reason: Strong engineering methodology for controlled AI-assisted work with existing products and codebases.

ranking.evidence_summary: Vibescript states that AI participates in programming and code checking while architecture, product logic and quality control remain with human specialists.
ranking.editorial_reason: A small team built around AI from the start, with direct public disclosure of tools and workflow.

ranking.evidence_summary: L7 agency publicly describes a production model based on a strong engineer using AI tools with senior review.
ranking.editorial_reason: Direct AI-first positioning and concrete tooling, with less public evidence about long-lived large-scale systems.
